family.name: Product Marketing Manager
family.summary: A competitor launches a cheaper plan just before your feature launch: find where you really win in the win/loss data, choose the launch message, and cut the unprovable claims from a launch page.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where do we actually win?
stages.summary: Read win/loss data: the product wins mid-size deals on speed, not features, and loses large deals on security. Think aloud.

stages.title: The launch message
stages.summary: Choose the launch message after a competitor price cut. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two weeks after launch
stages.summary: Results of their message. Tests reading signals and adapting.

stages.title: Review the launch page draft
stages.summary: A launch page with unprovable claims, feature-first copy and the wrong audience. Think aloud.

stages.title: Launch email (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the launch email to customers and prospects with AI. Catches buzzwords and unprovable claims.

stages.title: A launch you ran
stages.summary: A real launch or positioning change. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the product marketing manager at **Shiftly**, which sells field-service scheduling software to operations heads. Your homepage says "The all-in-one platform for every team". You launch route optimisation in 3 weeks.
Yesterday Clearbook launched a plan 25% cheaper than yours. The CEO asks: "What's our launch message now?"

brief.caption: Win/loss interviews, last 40 deals
rows: Won: "live in 5 days, not months" (8 of 14). Lost: price (2 of 4).
Lost: security reviews and single sign-on (13 of 19).

items: Only 3 of the 17 wins mentioned the number of features.
Customers say the competitor takes 6 weeks to set up.
Sales says: "Large companies are where the money is. We should go after them."

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a product you love that explains itself badly.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Who do we win with, and why? Is "all-in-one platform for every team" the right positioning?** Use the win/loss data.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Lead with price: match the competitor’s new cheaper plan
Lead with how fast mid-size teams get set up and see value
Lead with the new feature and the AI story
Lead with security and scale to win large companies

prompt.text: **What does the launch lead with?** Pick one, write the headline, and say how the new feature fits it.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Lead with price: match the competitor’s new cheaper plan"

prompt.text: You matched the price. Clearbook cut again by 10%. Sign-ups are flat and Finance says margins dropped. Sales asks for another discount.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Lead with how fast mid-size teams get set up and see value"

prompt.text: Trial sign-ups are up 10%, but Sales complains: "Large prospects say we look like a small-company tool." One large prospect dropped out.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Lead with the new feature and the AI story"

prompt.text: Press coverage was good, but sign-ups dropped 9%. In calls, buyers ask "is the AI safe with our data?" and Sales can't answer.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Lead with security and scale to win large companies"

prompt.text: Large-company leads went up, but every one stalled at the security review because single sign-on isn't built yet. Mid-size sign-ups fell.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: The agency sent this launch page draft. **Name the problems, worst first, and why each hurts.** Then rewrite the headline and first line.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: **Headline:** "India's #1 field-service scheduling software, now 10x smarter with route optimisation."
**Subhead:** "Built for the world's largest enterprises."
**Body:** "Powered by next-generation generative AI and a cutting-edge, cloud-native microservices architecture with 200+ features."
**Button:** "Book a demo".
**Footer:** a logo strip of 6 real customers (all have agreed).

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the launch email for route optimisation (subject line plus under 150 words) to mid-size operations heads.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a launch or positioning change you led, and how you knew whether it worked.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
